Two final contract choices remain:

1. **Late provider success after day-30 failure:** I recommend keeping the failure terminal, recording the discrepancy, and alerting admins for manual resolution. This follows the terminal-state rule you chose, but it means a simulated paid payment may remain unfulfilled until resolved.
2. **Checkout retries:** I recommend requiring an `Idempotency-Key`. Reusing the key returns the same attempt; a new key after failure starts a new attempt on the same cart.

I’ll write the API Service document after these are settled.

> # Message Queue Service Implementation Document
>
> ## Summary
>
> Create `Message_Queue_Service_Implementation.md` for the Message Queue Service alone. It will specify an email-only TypeScript service with one business endpoint, `POST /jobs`, a Workmatic queue in persistent `jobs.db`, and SMTP delivery to Mailpit. It will cover the service’s features, failure behavior, test gates, and deployment gates without specifying other services’ internals.
>
> ## Service contract and behavior
>
> - `POST /jobs` accepts a service-authenticated email job containing one recipient, an API-rendered subject and required text body, optional HTML, and a notification key for correlation. The sender address comes from queue configuration. Validate sizes and addresses; reject attachments and caller-supplied SMTP headers.
> - Return `202` and a Workmatic job ID only after `client.add()` persists the job. Use `401` for failed authentication, `400`/`422` for invalid input, `413` for oversized bodies, and `503` when durable enqueue fails. Reusing a notification key **may create another job and email**; there is no queue-side deduplication guarantee.
> - Add internal liveness and readiness routes as exceptions to the single business endpoint. Readiness checks the queue database and worker initialization; an SMTP outage does not prevent durable job acceptance.
> - Send through Mailpit SMTP with two concurrent workers. Use three total attempts for transient SMTP or network failures, with delays of 5 then 10 seconds; set SMTP timeout to 10 seconds, worker timeout to 20 seconds, and lease to 30 seconds.
> - On a permanent SMTP rejection, log an error and resolve the handler without retrying. Workmatic will mark that job `done`, meaning handling ended rather than email delivery succeeded. Exhausted transient jobs remain in Workmatic’s `dead` state. Provide no dashboard, dead-job alerts, or manual replay workflow; retain job rows until an explicit demo-volume reset.
> - State the delivery guarantee plainly: Workmatic persists jobs before `add()` returns, but a crash or expired lease can replay processing, so an email may be sent twice. [Workmatic documents this as at-least-once processing.](https://github.com/litepacks/workmatic)
>
> ## Implementation and gates
>
> - Specify the Yarn workspace, Express server, authenticated internal network binding, configuration and secret validation, structured redacted logs, graceful shutdown, and one persistent `jobs.db` volume. Workmatic owns its internal tables; the prestart command initializes them and runs Knex migrations for any queue-owned tables. Application SQL, if needed, uses parameterized `knex.raw`.
> - Define test gates for request authentication and validation; durable `202` acknowledgement; database failure; Mailpit acceptance; transient retry timing and exhaustion; permanent rejection with one attempt and an error log; duplicate submissions; restart and lease replay; health behavior; and graceful shutdown. Use temporary SQLite files and a real Mailpit container for integration tests.
> - Define deployment gates for an exact patch-pinned Alpine Node image, native SQLite dependency build, non-root runtime, persistent-volume permissions and backup, prestart initialization, health checks, Compose email smoke test, SMTP outage and recovery test, restart test, disk-capacity check, and README instructions. Production rollback preserves `jobs.db`; no production down migration or automatic job deletion.
> - Record an **integration blocker**: before API-to-queue acceptance, update the existing API Service implementation document and checklist to remove their queue deduplication promise and state that a lost enqueue acknowledgement can produce duplicate emails. This queue document will describe that dependency without implementing changes to the API Service.
>
> ## Assumptions
>
> The service runs only in the trusted assessment environment. The API Service renders email content; the queue validates and transports it. Mailpit SMTP acceptance is treated as successful delivery for this simulation. Duplicate email after uncertain SMTP acceptance is an accepted consequence of at-least-once delivery.

</details>

One library detail affects the permanent-failure rule: [Workmatic’s worker](https://github.com/litepacks/workmatic/blob/main/src/worker.ts) retries a thrown error until the job reaches its attempt limit; a handler that returns normally marks the job done. I found no per-error “dead immediately” path in that worker. I’ll settle how to record a permanent SMTP rejection without spending the remaining attempts.

> # Frontend Service Implementation Document
>
> ## Summary
>
> Create `Frontend_Service_Implementation.md` for the React single-page application only. It will define the five architecture routes, shopping and payment flows, failure-simulation controls, accessibility, tests, and deployment gates. Other services appear only as dependencies and interface contracts.
>
> ## Implementation
>
> - Use TypeScript, Vite, React Router, and shadcn/ui. Use direct `fetch` calls and React state; do not add a client data cache or service worker cache. Fetch fresh API data on route entry, relevant actions, SSE events, provider messages, reconnect, and manual refresh. Do not poll payment status. Static assets may use normal caching; runtime configuration must be fetched fresh.
> - Build `/login` around the API’s seeded-user list, showing each role. Store the selected user and Bearer token in local storage. On expiry or `401`, clear the session and ask the user to select a user again; do not silently renew. A global **Switch user** action revokes the old token when possible, clears in-flight requests and SSE, and starts the new session. No separate logout button is required.
> - Implement `/` redirect, paginated `/products`, `/payments`, and `/payments/:id`. Products includes active-cart add/update/remove/abandon actions, server-calculated totals, checkout, and links to retryable carts. Payment lists show only the data returned for the current role; admins see the system-wide list. Payment detail shows attempts, fulfilment, incidents safe for that viewer, manual refresh, and a same-cart retry after failure or cancellation using a **new** idempotency key.
> - Show API-provided provider scenarios and visible client demo controls to every seeded user. The double-checkout control sends concurrent requests with distinct keys; the timeout control aborts and retries with the **same** key; the SSE-disconnect control pauses and reconnects the stream, then refetches. Keep client and provider scenarios mutually exclusive for one checkout. Test API-crash cases outside the UI.
> - Keep checkout and the iframe dialog on `/products`. Persist the key for an uncertain checkout request so a retry reuses it. Open a returned provider URL only after checking it against the configured provider origin. A `202` response without a URL shows an initialization state and manual refresh/retry with the same key.
> - Embed the provider URL in an accessible dialog with a restricted iframe, no token sharing, and an **Open in new tab** fallback. The provider must allow the frontend origin to frame its page, and the frontend must allow the provider origin in `frame-src`; these are distinct policies. [Browser framing policy reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/frame-ancestors).
> - Accept a provider `postMessage` only from the configured origin and active iframe, with a matching payment reference. Treat it as a hint: close the dialog immediately, refetch the API, and show a pending banner if the API has not confirmed a terminal state. SSE uses an Authorization-capable fetch stream; each status event and reconnect triggers a fresh payment read. A disconnected stream shows a reconnect/manual-refresh affordance without polling.
> - Put browser-reachable API, provider, documentation, and Mailpit origins in runtime configuration generated when the frontend container starts. Provide global links to documentation and Mailpit in new tabs. The API must serve fresh data without a server-side data cache.
>
> ## Test and deployment gates
>
> - Test route guards, stored-session expiry and user switching, role-specific payment views, cart operations, pagination, checkout key reuse/new-key retry, `202` initialization, and API error states with mocked contracts.
> - Test iframe URL allowlisting, framing fallback, dialog keyboard/focus behavior, `postMessage` origin/source/reference rejection, pending-after-message behavior, and confirmation from fresh API state. Test SSE event, disconnect/reconnect, manual refresh, and absence of periodic polling or client data caching.
> - Run browser end-to-end flows against Compose: seeded login → cart → checkout → embedded provider → verified payment; failed/cancelled retry; provider scenarios; concurrent checkout; client timeout replay; SSE disconnect; admin payment listing; documentation and Mailpit links. Include responsive and accessibility checks.
> - Build one static frontend container from exact patch-pinned Alpine images, with a SPA route fallback, non-root runtime, startup-generated runtime config, and health check. Gate deployment on typecheck, lint, unit/integration and browser tests, image build, browser-reachable origins, API CORS, provider framing headers, CSP, and Compose smoke tests. Document setup, scenario walkthrough, test commands, and known demo-only authentication limits.
>
> ## Assumptions
>
> The app runs in the trusted assessment demo. Local storage preserves the selected session across reloads, but an expired token requires user selection. The provider implements the agreed framing and `postMessage` contract; the API remains authoritative for payment status. No client or API data cache and no periodic payment polling are added.

> # Mock Email Service implementation document
>
> ## Summary
>
> Create `Mock_Email_Service_Implementation.md` for the Mailpit container only. It will define how the service captures email from the Message Queue Service and exposes its inbox to a browser on the trusted Compose host. The API owns recipients and email content; the queue owns job persistence and SMTP retries.
>
> ## Implementation and interfaces
>
> - Build Mailpit **v1.33.1 from its pinned upstream source** in a multi-stage Dockerfile using `alpine:3.24.4` for both build and runtime stages. Verify the source revision, use the upstream lockfile and build steps, record the resulting image digest, and run the final container as a non-root user. Mailpit’s [source instructions](https://mailpit.axllent.org/docs/install/source/) and [upstream Dockerfile](https://github.com/axllent/mailpit/blob/develop/Dockerfile) establish the required Go, npm, UI, and binary build steps.
> - Run one Mailpit container. Listen on Compose-network SMTP port `1025` without authentication or TLS; do not publish SMTP to the host. Publish the UI/API port `8025` on `127.0.0.1` only. Set the frontend’s browser-reachable `MAILPIT_ORIGIN` to `http://127.0.0.1:8025`. The frontend opens that URL in a new tab; it makes no Mailpit API calls.
> - Persist `/data/mailpit.db` in a named local volume. Set `MP_MAX_MESSAGES=0` and leave `MP_MAX_AGE` unset so messages remain until an explicit disposable-volume reset. Keep duplicate-ID filtering off so repeated SMTP deliveries remain visible. Limit accepted messages to 1 MB and check volume capacity during deployment. Mailpit’s [storage documentation](https://mailpit.axllent.org/docs/configuration/email-storage/) explains its temporary database and default 500-message pruning.
> - Keep SMTP relay, forwarding, POP3, Chaos, and external version checks disabled. Use a Mailpit host-header allowlist for its Compose name; loopback hosts are permitted by Mailpit. Keep the UI/API unauthenticated only under the agreed host-local, trusted-demo deployment. Do not enable browser CORS for the frontend link. Mailpit’s [HTTP configuration](https://mailpit.axllent.org/docs/configuration/http/) defines the host allowlist.
> - Use Mailpit’s `/livez` and `/readyz` endpoints for health checks. A successful SMTP acceptance means the message was captured; it does not mean delivery to a real mailbox. The service adds no custom business routes or notification logic. [Mailpit healthcheck documentation](https://mailpit.axllent.org/docs/integration/healthcheck/).
>
> ## Test gates
>
> - **Build and configuration:** Verify pinned source and Alpine versions, reproducible build, non-root runtime, writable data volume, expected listeners, disabled relay/forwarding/Chaos, and the absence of published SMTP or unintended CORS.
> - **Capture and inbox:** Send text and HTML messages through the real queue-to-Mailpit SMTP path; verify sender, recipient, subject, bodies, and separate copies of duplicate deliveries through Mailpit’s documented API and UI. Verify the frontend link opens the host-local inbox.
> - **Persistence and failure:** Restart Mailpit and confirm captured messages remain. Verify an unwritable or full data volume fails readiness or SMTP acceptance visibly. Stop Mailpit, confirm the queue observes an SMTP outage, then restore it and confirm eligible queued jobs reach the inbox. SMTP 4xx/5xx classification belongs in the queue’s tests using a test SMTP server; this deployment has **no SMTP error injection**.
> - **End-to-end acceptance:** Confirm expected user and admin notification emails appear after the relevant payment outcomes, while payment processing remains independent of inbox availability. Record each test command, result, and any unrun gate.
>
> ## Deployment gates and assumptions
>
> - **D1 — Artifact:** Build and inspect the single source-built, patch-pinned Alpine image; record source revision and image digest.
> - **D2 — Storage and exposure:** Verify volume ownership, free space, host-loopback UI binding, internal-only SMTP, and the frontend’s browser URL. Take a consistent backup before upgrading an existing inbox.
> - **D3 — Readiness:** Start the single container; require healthy `/livez` and `/readyz`, a reachable browser UI, and an internal SMTP connection.
> - **D4 — Functional and recovery smoke:** Capture a queue email, inspect it in the UI, restart Mailpit, confirm persistence, and exercise SMTP outage and restoration.
> - **D5 — Operations:** Document start/stop, inbox access, health checks, logs, backup/restore, disk monitoring, and an **explicit** reset of the disposable Mailpit volume. Preserve the database on rollback; restore a pre-upgrade backup if an older Mailpit version cannot read the upgraded database.
>
> The deployment is restricted to a trusted demo host. Captured messages are retained until an intentional reset, and Mailpit never relays them to real recipients.

> # Mock Payment Provider Service implementation document
>
> ## Summary
>
> Create `Mock_Payment_Provider_Service_Implementation.md` for the provider alone. It will specify payment initialization, a token-protected checkout page, authoritative simulated payment state, signed webhook delivery, failure scenarios, persistence, and test and deployment gates. The API retains responsibility for cart state, payment verification, fulfilment, reconciliation, and notifications.
>
> The architecture’s `POST /payments` wording is superseded by the agreed routes: the API calls `POST /payments/initialise`; the provider’s checkout page calls `POST /payments/submit`.
>
> ## Interfaces and payment lifecycle
>
> - **Server routes:** Require `Authorization: Bearer <PROVIDER_SERVICE_SECRET>` for `POST /payments/initialise`, `GET /payments/:reference`, and `GET /failure-scenarios`. Initialization accepts the API-generated reference, positive minor-unit amount, `NGN` currency, fixed `checkout_expires_at`, and optional active scenario code. Return the provider reference, status, payment URL, and cutoff. The same reference and identical details return the existing transaction and URL; conflicting details return `409`. Status lookup is read-only and reports provider truth even if webhooks failed.
> - **Browser routes:** `GET /checkout/:token` renders the provider-owned payment page. It displays the fixed amount/reference and Pay, Fail, and Cancel actions. The page submits `checkout_token` and `outcome` to `POST /payments/submit` on the provider origin. Generate an unguessable token for the payment URL, validate it on submission, and never accept browser-supplied amount, reference, or callback URL. A pending payment can transition once to `success`, `failed`, or `cancelled`; repeat submission of its completed outcome is harmless, while a conflicting outcome is rejected.
> - **Expiry:** The API supplies one immutable cutoff at initialization. After that time, block a still-pending browser checkout with an expired-page response while leaving provider status `pending` for the API’s day-30 lookup. Previously completed payments remain readable. Verify the API’s defensive late-success discrepancy path with an isolated test fixture, without a runtime mutation route.
> - **Frontend handoff:** Make the page usable in the frontend iframe and as a standalone tab. Permit only the configured frontend origin through `frame-ancestors`, with no conflicting `X-Frame-Options` header. After completion, send only `postMessage({ type: 'mock-payment.finished', reference })` to the exact frontend origin; the message is a refresh hint, not payment proof. Use no-store responses, a restrictive CSP, no-referrer policy, accessible controls, and logs that redact checkout tokens. [Framing policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/frame-ancestors) and [postMessage origin handling](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/postMessage) must be verified in a real browser.
> - **Webhook contract:** Persist the provider outcome and immutable event record before attempting delivery to the API’s fixed internal webhook URL. Sign the exact transmitted body with HMAC-SHA-256 using `PROVIDER_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and send `X-Provider-Signature: sha256=<hex>`. Include stable `event_id`, type/status, reference, provider reference, amount, currency, and occurrence time. Reuse event IDs and bytes on retries unless the selected scenario deliberately alters the transmitted body or signature. Never provide a browser or API route that directly confirms a payment for the API.
>
> ## Storage, delivery, and scenarios
>
> - Keep provider-owned `payments`, `webhook_events`, `webhook_deliveries`, and seeded `failure_scenarios` in persistent `payment_provider.db`. Add the token, cutoff, scenario snapshot, and dispatch metadata needed by the agreed behavior. Use Knex migrations and parameterized `knex.raw` for provider-owned runtime queries. Workmatic uses **the same database file** and owns its internal tables; initialize those tables before serving traffic. The event table serves as a durable outbox, so a crash between committing an outcome and adding a Workmatic job cannot lose the webhook. A crash after job creation may produce an extra delivery, which the API handles by event ID. [Workmatic’s persistence and lease model](https://github.com/litepacks/workmatic) is at least once.
> - Run one provider container and webhook worker. Record every HTTP attempt in `webhook_deliveries`. Retry network errors, timeouts, HTTP `5xx`, `408`, and `429` up to five total attempts with 2/4/8/16-second backoff. Stop on API `2xx` or permanent `4xx`; retain exhausted or permanently rejected events and attempts for inspection. A permanent rejection may leave Workmatic’s job `done` while the provider event is `failed`. Do not add a manual replay control; the API’s status reconciliation is the recovery path.
> - Seed the architecture’s active scenarios: `PROVIDER_001` delays **before** persistence for 30 seconds; `PROVIDER_002` returns HTTP `500` without persistence; `WEBHOOK_001/002` send concurrent/sequential duplicates; `003` delays delivery; `004` skips it; `008` sends a valid success event, then a conflicting failed event after the first is acknowledged; `011` transmits an amount increased by 1,000; `013` sends an invalid signature; and `016` sends malformed, correctly signed JSON. `WEBHOOK_008` permits only the Pay action and keeps provider truth `success`. Snapshot scenario configuration at initialization. Expose active code/name/description/category through the authenticated catalogue; provide no runtime scenario-editing API.
> - Keep the separate “response lost after creation” case in the integration test harness: drop the initialization response after the provider commits, then verify lookup and same-reference retry recover the existing transaction. Do not add it to the demo catalogue.
>
> ## Test and deployment gates
>
> - **Tests:** Require build/lint/type checks; migration, constraint, seed, and restart tests on file-backed SQLite; service authentication and validation; same-reference idempotency and conflict; token authorization, one-way terminal transitions, expiry, and accessible iframe/new-tab checkout. Exercise every seeded scenario, exact webhook bytes/signatures, duplicate and conflicting events, durable outbox crash windows, Workmatic lease replay, retry exhaustion, and permanent rejection. In Compose, verify API reconciliation after missing or rejected webhooks, one fulfilment despite duplicates, the late-success defensive fixture, and browser `postMessage`/framing behavior. Record each command, result, and unrun suite.
> - **Deployment:** Build one non-root container from an exact patch-pinned Alpine image; build native SQLite dependencies for the runtime platform and record the image digest. Run provider `up` migrations and Workmatic initialization before starting the service; never run production `down` migrations. Verify secrets, fixed API callback URL, browser-reachable provider origin, frontend framing origin, volume ownership, free space, and a consistent pre-upgrade backup. Require database/worker readiness, initialization/status/catalogue checks, browser checkout, signed webhook smoke, outage/restart recovery, and scenario smoke before acceptance. Preserve the database and logs on rollback; restore a verified backup if the previous image cannot read the upgraded schema. Document local operation, scenario walkthroughs, logs, backup/restore, and test commands in the README.
>
> ## Cross-service contract to align
>
> Before integration acceptance, update the API Service document and checklist to call `POST /payments/initialise`, pass immutable `checkout_expires_at`, and retry provider HTTP `500` as a transient initialization failure. The provider document will describe these as interface dependencies; it will contain no API, frontend, or queue implementation tasks.

</details>

> # API Documentation Service implementation document
>
> ## Summary
>
> Create `API_Documentation_Service_Implementation.md` for the standalone Swagger UI service. It will render the API Service’s live OpenAPI document, provide an interactive trusted-demo client, and include a seeded-user picker. The API Service owns the OpenAPI content and all payment behavior; this service owns presentation, browser configuration, and documentation-specific access controls.
>
> ## Interface and user experience
>
> - On each page load and explicit **Refresh specification**, fetch `GET <API_ORIGIN>/v1/api_docs.json` directly from the browser with `cache: 'no-store'`. Show a retryable error if unavailable; use no bundled stale fallback. Validate the OpenAPI document and require every effective server URL to resolve to the configured browser `API_ORIGIN`. A mismatch blocks Try it out with a configuration error.
> - Render the live document with a pinned `swagger-ui-dist` release. Keep normal API operations interactive, including cart mutations and checkout. Display a notice that Try it out changes persistent demo data. Document the webhook and SSE operations but disable their execution controls; also disable manual execution of login/logout because the picker is the sole identity control. Use a version-pinned Swagger UI plugin for those operation controls and a request interceptor that blocks dispatch to those paths if the UI control fails. Swagger UI’s standard submit-method setting is global, while its [plugin API](https://swagger.io/docs/open-source-tools/swagger-ui/customization/plugin-api/) permits component customization.
> - Fetch active seeded users from `GET /v1/demo/users`, showing names and roles. Selection calls `POST /v1/login`; store the returned token and selected profile in this documentation origin’s **local storage**. Inject that token into protected Try it out requests. On **Switch user**, best-effort call `POST /v1/logout`, clear local credentials and the checkout-key helper, then show the picker. An API `401` clears credentials and requests a new selection. Keep the documentation view available without a selected user.
> - Add a **Generate/copy checkout key** helper. Persist its current random `Idempotency-Key` for the selected user across reloads; explain when to reuse it after an uncertain response and when to generate a new key for a new attempt. The API’s OpenAPI operation must declare the required header. Users open the returned provider payment URL separately to complete checkout.
> - Serve a small runtime configuration containing only browser-reachable `API_ORIGIN`; do not bundle a Compose hostname or secret. Allow requests only to that origin. Set `validatorUrl: null`, `queryConfigEnabled: false`, `persistAuthorization: false`, and `withCredentials: false`; the custom picker is the only token store. Swagger UI otherwise defaults to an [external validator](https://swagger.io/docs/open-source-tools/swagger-ui/usage/configuration/).
>
> ## Build and service behavior
>
> - Use one multi-stage Dockerfile and one non-root static-serving container. Pin `swagger-ui-dist` through the workspace lockfile, copy its assets and the custom shell into Nginx on `alpine:3.24.4`, and record the built image digest. Add no service database or migrations. [Swagger UI supports serving its distribution as static assets.](https://swagger.io/docs/open-source-tools/swagger-ui/usage/installation/)
> - Publish the docs origin on host loopback for the trusted demo. Serve runtime config and HTML without stale caching; cache versioned static assets normally. Use a CSP limited to local scripts/styles and the configured API connection, with no third-party validator or CDN assets.
> - Add internal liveness and readiness checks for static serving and valid runtime config. An API outage leaves the docs container running but produces a clear spec-load error. The frontend’s configured `DOCS_ORIGIN` opens this UI in a new tab.
>
> ## Test and deployment gates
>
> - **Static/contract:** Validate the build, lockfile, Alpine pin, non-root image, runtime config, and all documentation-service assets. Confirm the live OpenAPI document covers the API routes, Bearer scheme, webhook HMAC description, checkout `Idempotency-Key`, request/response examples, and a browser-reachable API server URL.
> - **Browser behavior:** Test fresh spec load/refresh, API outage/retry, invalid or mismatched server URLs, seeded user/admin selection, local-storage reload, token expiry, switch-user revocation attempt, and protected Try it out requests. Confirm checkout-key reuse/new-key instructions and a real checkout request.
> - **Execution limits/security:** Verify webhook, SSE, login, and logout remain visible but cannot be dispatched through Swagger UI; the interceptor also blocks direct UI execution attempts. Confirm no request reaches an external validator or arbitrary spec/API URL, no token appears in a URL or logs, and API CORS permits only the configured docs origin and required methods/headers.
> - **Compose end-to-end:** From the docs UI, select a seeded user, create or inspect a cart, submit checkout with a generated key, open the provider URL, and inspect the API-confirmed payment. Test desktop and narrow layouts, keyboard navigation, error announcements, and the frontend’s docs link.
> - **Deployment:** Gate configuration and API CORS first; then artifact and static checks; then container readiness and browser connectivity; then functional, outage, and security smokes. Document local start/stop, runtime origins, user selection, checkout-key use, Try it out limitations, test commands, and rollback. Record each gate’s command/result and every unrun check. Roll back by restoring the previous static image and matching runtime config; this service has no data migration.
>
> ## Assumptions and cross-service contract
>
> This is a host-local trusted demo; passwordless selection includes admins and local-storage tokens. Before integration acceptance, the API’s OpenAPI output must advertise the configured browser `API_ORIGIN` at every applicable server level and accurately describe Bearer, HMAC, and `Idempotency-Key` requirements. The documentation service will report contract mismatches rather than rewrite the API specification.

> # Deployment and Documentation Implementation Document
>
> ## Summary
>
> Create `Deployment_and_Documentation_Implementation.md` as the **root integration plan** for the six services in `System_Architecture.md`. It will cover Compose deployment, shared configuration, data protection, the root README, and assessment submission gates. Service internals and their existing test gates remain in their own implementation documents.
>
> ## Deployment design
>
> - Define one Docker Compose service and one Dockerfile per microservice. Build every runtime image from an exact patch-pinned Alpine base, record its digest, and run the six regular containers as non-root users. Temporary migration containers use the corresponding service images and leave no seventh long-running service.
> - Use one named volume for `api.db`, `jobs.db`, and `payment_provider.db`, with separate service-owned directories and distinct non-root user IDs. Each service accesses only its own database. Keep Mailpit’s inbox on a separate named volume.
> - Provide a root Yarn/Commander deployment command. It validates configuration, builds images, prepares volume permissions, takes a backup when data exists, runs API migrations, provider migrations/seeds and Workmatic initialization, and queue initialization through sequential `docker compose run --rm --no-deps` commands. Only after those succeed does it start the six services. Production `down` migrations are prohibited. [Docker’s one-off command reference](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/run/) supports this flow.
> - Use host-loopback browser origins and internal Compose DNS for service calls. Set default host ports to frontend `8080`, API `3000`, provider `3001`, docs `8081`, and Mailpit UI `8025`; do not publish queue HTTP or Mailpit SMTP. Supply the API’s public origin so its OpenAPI server URL matches the browser URL used by the docs UI. Health checks test each service’s own readiness without making recoverable dependency outages crash unrelated services.
>
> ## Operations and documentation
>
> - Specify a **cold backup** of the shared volume: stop the API, queue, and provider writers, copy the entire volume including SQLite WAL files, then restart and verify readiness. Document restoration into an isolated volume before switching over. A reset command must target an explicitly disposable Compose project and named volumes; ordinary stop/start preserves data. [Docker’s volume guidance](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/volumes/) covers backup and restore.
> - Require a root README with architecture summary, prerequisites, configuration and secret-file setup, start/stop commands, browser URLs, seeded-user selection, cart-to-provider payment walkthrough, failure-scenario instructions, API/docs/Mailpit links, test commands, logs, backup/restore, and known demo limitations. Explain the deliberate absence of a client payment-status update route.
> - Add an assessment submission gate for the repository URL, reviewed incremental Conventional Commit history, and a **separate full AI-work transcript artifact** containing prompts and responses. The README names that artifact and explains how it accompanies the submission; credentials must be removed before sharing it.
>
> ## Verification and acceptance gates
>
> - Validate rendered Compose configuration, exact image pins and digests, six-container topology, loopback-only published ports, internal-only queue/SMTP access, secret handling, distinct database permissions, and browser/internal origin consistency.
> - Run each service’s existing test gates with disposable data: Japa v5 for the API, queue, and provider; the documented frontend and static-service checks for the remaining services. A root Compose end-to-end gate verifies success, failure, cancellation, selected failure scenarios, API-confirmed payment state, email capture, docs access, and recovery after provider, queue, or Mailpit outages.
> - Gate deployment in order on configuration, artifacts and tests, backup, prestart initialization, health, functional smoke, recovery smoke, and README/runbook review. Record commands, results, and every unrun gate. Separately verify transcript completeness and commit history before assessment submission.
>
> ## Settled defaults
>
> This is a trusted, host-local demo. The three application SQLite databases share one volume for easier backup; Mailpit uses its own. Backups stop writers. Migrations run in temporary Compose containers before regular services start. The AI transcript is delivered as a separate submission artifact.

> Within each workspace, setup Japa with an entry point file (bin/test.ts). Then setup suites within the entry point file. The integration suite should run migrations and seeder within the before hook and in the hook return function so that each test runs on a fresh database. Then refactor the tests and remove the database setups within the tests. Database should be provisioned centrally within the entrypoint. This should be documented in the AGENTS.md.&#x20;
>
> The HTTP servers needed within the integration tests should be provisioned within the entrypoint file too.
>
> See [https://japa.dev/docs/installation](https://japa.dev/docs/installation)
>
> Use test macros expose common functionalities within test contexts. [https://japa.dev/docs/test-macros](https://japa.dev/docs/test-macros)
>
> Register the api client centrally via the entrypoint file [https://japa.dev/docs/plugins/api-client.](https://japa.dev/docs/plugins/api-client.) Same for the assert plugin [https://japa.dev/docs/plugins/assert](https://japa.dev/docs/plugins/assert);&#x20;
>
> Use per test lifecycle hooks to finer control of before and after hook processes: [https://japa.dev/docs/lifecycle-hooks](https://japa.dev/docs/lifecycle-hooks)
>
> I’ll incorporate this test-harness standard into the active implementation. For the API workspace, I’ll move disposable database and HTTP-fixture setup into the Japa entry point, register the API client and assertion plugins there, and expose shared setup through macros. I’ll also document the pattern in `AGENTS.md` and apply it to each service workspace as it is built.

'Keep skipped events `skipped` with no delivery job; allow API reconciliation to recover the provider outcome.',

'**Initialization scenarios:** `PROVIDER_001` first times out/looks absent then resolves to one payment; `PROVIDER_002` creates none; a test proxy drops a committed response and lookup recovers the same row.',

> cat > services/frontend/README.md <<'EOF'
>
> # Frontend Service
>
> This is the trusted local assessment storefront. It uses a passwordless seeded-user selector, stores the selected Bearer token in this browser origin's local storage, reads API data directly without caching it, and treats API payment reads as authoritative. Never expose the demo to untrusted users.
>
> ## Local development
>
> From the repository root:
>
> ```sh
> yarn workspace @executivepros/frontend dev
> ```
>
> The Vite server uses browser origins on ports `18083` (API), `18082` (provider), `18081` (API docs), and `18025` (Mailpit) unless overridden in the environment. The generated `public/config.json` is development-only, ignored by Git, and removed before a production build. Do not put credentials in those origins or this file.
>
> ## Compose
>
> Compose publishes the frontend at `http://127.0.0.1:18080`; runtime config provides browser-reachable origins for API, provider, docs, and Mailpit. Start and inspect the service from the repository root:
>
> ```sh
> docker compose up -d frontend
> docker compose stop frontend
> docker compose logs --tail=100 frontend
> ```
>
> The seeded-user token and pending checkout intent stay in local storage on the frontend origin. Switching users attempts API revocation, then clears the token and intent even when logout is unavailable. Checkout mutations are persistent demo data. Checkout keys are stored before requests and reused after uncertain outcomes. A provider message is only a hint; the frontend displays success, failure, or cancellation after a fresh API read. The new-tab checkout fallback is available if the iframe cannot load.
>
> The frontend makes no payment database changes and has no migration. Rollback restores the prior static image and matching runtime origins; it does not alter API payment data.
>
> ## Gates
>
> ```sh
> yarn workspace @executivepros/frontend lint
> yarn workspace @executivepros/frontend typecheck
> yarn workspace @executivepros/frontend test:unit
> yarn workspace @executivepros/frontend test:integration
> yarn workspace @executivepros/frontend build
> FRONTEND_TEST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080 yarn workspace @executivepros/frontend test:e2e
> ```
>
> Unit and integration tests use Vitest, Testing Library, and MSW. Playwright is a real-browser test and must target a disposable Compose project/database; it creates a cart and payment. Do not point it at a developer's persistent demo database. Include test logs and leave every unrun gate open in `Frontend_Service_Implementation_Todo.md`.

import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process'
const names=['e2e-restore-2-api-1','e2e-restore-2-provider-1','e2e-restore-2-queue-1','e2e-restore-2-mailpit-1']
const started=new Set()
const stop=name=>{execFileSync('docker',['stop',name],{stdio:'ignore'});started.delete(name)}
const start=name=>{execFileSync('docker',['start',name],{stdio:'ignore'});started.add(name)}
const status=async url=>{const response=await fetch(url,{signal:AbortSignal.timeout(5000)});if(response.status!==200)throw new Error(url+' returned '+response.status);return response.status}
try{
 stop(names[1]);stop(names[2]);
 const apiReady=await status('http://127.0.0.1:18483/health/ready')
 start(names[1]);start(names[2]);
 stop(names[0]);
 const providerReady=await status('http://127.0.0.1:18482/health/ready')
 start(names[0]);
 stop(names[3]);
 const queue=execFileSync('docker',['exec',names[2],'node','-e',"fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/health/ready').then(r=>{console.log(r.status);if(r.status!==200)process.exit(1)}).catch(()=>process.exit(2))"],{encoding:'utf8'}).trim()
 if(queue!=='200')throw new Error('queue readiness returned '+queue)
 start(names[3]);
 console.log(JSON.stringify({api_ready_without_provider_or_queue:apiReady,provider_ready_without_api:providerReady,queue_ready_without_smtp:Number(queue)}))
}finally{for(const name of names)if(!started.has(name)){try{start(name)}catch{}}}

import {randomUUID} from 'node:crypto'
const api='http://127.0.0.1:18483'
const req=async(url,init)=>{const response=await fetch(url,init);const text=await response.text();let body;try{body=text?JSON.parse(text):null}catch{body=text}if(!response.ok)throw new Error(`${init?.method??'GET'} ${url} returned ${response.status}: ${JSON.stringify(body)}`);return body}
const sleep=ms=>new Promise(resolve=>setTimeout(resolve,ms))
const users=await req(api+'/v1/demo/users'),user=users.data.find(x=>x.role==='user')
const login=await req(api+'/v1/login',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({user_id:user.id})})
const auth='Bearer '+login.data.token,headers={authorization:auth,'content-type':'application/json'}
const products=(await req(api+'/v1/products',{headers})).data,product=products.find(x=>x.available_stock>0)
if(!product)throw new Error('No seeded product has available stock')
await req(api+'/v1/cart',{method:'POST',headers,body:JSON.stringify({items:[{product_id:product.id,quantity:1}]})})
const checkout=(await req(api+'/v1/cart/checkout',{method:'POST',headers:{...headers,'idempotency-key':randomUUID()},body:JSON.stringify({failure_scenario_code:'WEBHOOK_004'})})).data
if(!checkout.payment_url)throw new Error('No provider URL for skipped-webhook scenario')
const paymentUrl=new URL(checkout.payment_url)
const outcome=await fetch(paymentUrl.origin+'/payments/submit',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'},body:new URLSearchParams({checkout_token:paymentUrl.pathname.split('/').at(-1),outcome:'success'})})
if(!outcome.ok)throw new Error('Provider action returned '+outcome.status)
let payment
for(let attempt=0;attempt<105;attempt++){await sleep(1000);payment=(await req(api+'/v1/payments/'+checkout.id,{headers:{authorization:auth}})).data;if(payment.status==='success')break}
if(payment?.status!=='success')throw new Error('API did not recover skipped webhook; state='+(payment?.status??'missing'))
console.log(JSON.stringify({missing_webhook_reconciled:true,payment_status:payment.status,fulfillment_present:!!payment.fulfillment,incident_count:payment.incidents.length,payment_id:checkout.id}))
NODE``

if(payment.status!=='cancelled')throw new Error('Cleanup did not confirm cancellation')
console.log(JSON.stringify({invalid_signature_http:forged.status,forged_success_left_state: 'pending',final_cleanup_status:payment.status,fulfillment_present:!!payment.fulfillment}))

const req=async(url,init)=>{const response=await fetch(url,init);const text=await response.text();let body;try{body=text?JSON.parse(text):null}catch{body=text}return {status:response.status,body}}
const sleep=ms=>new Promise(resolve=>setTimeout(resolve,ms))

const products=(await req(api+'/v1/products',{headers})).body.data,product=products.find(x=>x.available_stock>0)
if(!product)throw new Error('No seeded product has available stock')
await req(api+'/v1/cart',{method:'POST',headers,body:JSON.stringify({items:[{product_id:product.id,quantity:1}]})})
const key=randomUUID()
const checkout=await req(api+'/v1/cart/checkout',{method:'POST',headers:{...headers,'idempotency-key':key},body:JSON.stringify({failure_scenario_code:'PROVIDER_001'})})
if(checkout.status!==202||checkout.body.data.payment_url!==null)throw new Error('Delayed initialization should return 202 without a URL, got '+checkout.status)
await sleep(32000)
const replay=await req(api+'/v1/cart/checkout',{method:'POST',headers:{...headers,'idempotency-key':key},body:JSON.stringify({failure_scenario_code:'PROVIDER_001'})})
if(replay.status!==200||replay.body.data.id!==checkout.body.data.id||!replay.body.data.payment_url)throw new Error('Same-key replay did not resolve to the original ready payment: HTTP '+replay.status)
const serviceSecret=readFileSync('.local/secrets/provider_service_secret','utf8').trim()
const providerPayment=await req(provider+'/payments/'+encodeURIComponent(replay.body.data.reference),{headers:{authorization:'Bearer '+serviceSecret}})
if(providerPayment.status!==200||providerPayment.body.data.reference!==replay.body.data.reference)throw new Error('Provider status lookup did not resolve the original reference')
const detail=(await req(api+'/v1/payments/'+checkout.body.data.id,{headers:{authorization:auth}})).body.data
if(detail.status!=='pending'||detail.payment_url!==replay.body.data.payment_url)throw new Error('API payment detail did not expose the recovered URL')

const cancelled=await fetch(paymentUrl.origin+'/payments/submit',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'},body:new URLSearchParams({checkout_token:paymentUrl.pathname.split('/').at(-1),outcome:'cancelled'})})
if(!cancelled.ok)throw new Error('Provider cleanup cancellation returned '+cancelled.status)
let final=detail
for(let i=0;i<40;i++){await sleep(500);final=(await req(api+'/v1/payments/'+checkout.body.data.id,{headers:{authorization:auth}})).body.data;if(final.status==='cancelled')break}
if(final.status!=='cancelled')throw new Error('Provider cleanup cancellation did not transition API state')
console.log(JSON.stringify({delayed_provider_checkout_http:checkout.status,initial_url:null,replay_http:replay.status,same_payment_id:replay.body.data.id===checkout.body.data.id,provider_lookup:providerPayment.status,api_url_recovered:true,cleanup_status:final.status}))
NODE`

console.log(JSON.stringify({duplicate_webhook_scenario:true,payment_status:payment.status,single_fulfillment:!!payment.fulfillment,stock_decrement:stockBefore-productAfter.available_stock,duplicate_outcomes:diagnostics.data.webhook_outcomes.duplicate}))

The API now validates the candidate reference only to find a matching local payment, then links the incident using that payment’s stored reference. The unverified webhook still cannot change payment status or supply payment evidence.

> The trace points to a correlation gap: `WEBHOOK_016` sends bytes that cannot be parsed, so the API returns before it can find the payment reference or persist an incident. I’m fixing the webhook contract with a separately HMAC-bound reference header; that lets the API safely attach a malformed-payload incident to the payment without trusting an unsigned header or applying payload data.

Root cause: `WEBHOOK_016` sends syntactically malformed JSON. The API rejected it before it could read the payment reference, persist an incident, or report the rejection in the payment timeline.

The provider now sends a reference authenticated against the exact webhook body. When the API receives a validly signed malformed body, it records a deduplicated `malformed_webhook_json` incident and emits webhook receipt, verification, and rejection activity—without applying payment data. The new headers are documented in the API OpenAPI contract.

ESLint, formatting, and API/provider typechecks passed. I did not run test suites. Rebuild or restart the running services to load the change.

Committed as `51a2d94` (`fix: persist malformed provider webhook incidents`).

`yarn deploy:local` now creates `.env` from `.env.example` when missing, preserves an existing `.env`, generates or validates the secret files, writes their relative paths into `.env`, and then uses that file for Compose operations. Compose mounts the files at the existing `/run/secrets/...` container paths. I removed the manual copy instructions.

Updated the deployment docs and checklist, and added tests for first-run creation, preserving settings, concurrent startup, and invalid secret-path entries.

**Verified:** all 25 deployment tests pass; Docker Compose accepted the relative secret paths; Node syntax checks and `git diff --check` pass. I did not run a full deployment.

> The browser failure is a real timing gap: the provider can finish and publish the terminal SSE event before the checkout response assigns the payment ID to the page’s current intent. The notification is retained, but the page only reacts to the single latest event; it can miss the status refresh and remain visibly pending. I’m changing the page to reconcile against retained terminal notifications when the intent arrives, and I’ll add a browser regression that delays the checkout response to force that ordering.
